title: Player profiles and leaderboard on DynamoDB
name: Player rating store

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code models the data for its leaderboard query? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The leaderboard partition key is `LB#<season>#<0..7>` derived from the player id, and `topPlayers` queries all eight shards with `limit(n)` before merging. Why is querying every shard necessary?
choices: DynamoDB cannot run a Query against a global secondary index with a single partition key
Each shard holds an arbitrary subset of players, so the global top n may lie entirely in any one shard, and the best n of each shard must be merged
The shards hold different seasons, so all eight are needed to cover the current one
Eventually consistent index reads can miss a shard, so eight reads average out the errors

questions.prompt: The game server delivers the same MatchResult (same matchId and playedAtMillis) twice for one player. What does the second `recordMatch` call do?
choices: It adds a second match item and applies the rating change again
It overwrites the first match item and applies the rating change again
The match Put fails its attribute_not_exists condition, the whole transaction is cancelled including the rating update, and the method returns DUPLICATE
It retries up to three times and then throws ConcurrentUpdateException

questions.prompt: Two different matches of the same player finish at the same moment, and both calls read rating 1000 from the profile. What is the outcome?
choices: Both transactions commit; the last writer's rating wins and one rating change is lost
The first commits; the second is cancelled on the `rating = :old` condition, its match item is not written, and the retry reloads the new rating and applies its change on top
Both fail and ConcurrentUpdateException is thrown at once
The consistent read makes the second call wait until the first has finished
